analyst_reports.business_description: Twenty-year-old data-integration and analytics software vendor. ~55% of revenue from government / defense / intelligence agencies on multi-year contracts with very high switching costs and security-accreditation moats; the rest is commercial enterprise. Software is deployed against the customer's own sensitive data (ontology / pipeline layer), sold top-down, and usage expands within accounts over years. Founder-led, dual-class shares, famously mission-driven/contrarian culture. Heavy stock-based compensation is the main shareholder complaint.
recent_developments: First GAAP-profitable quarter in company history just reported (net income 93 on 1526 revenue); management guided the company's first full profitable YEAR for the new fiscal year, with GAAP profit guided alongside a 22%-margin adjusted-operating-income outlook.

Growth has DECELERATED for eight straight quarters (from ~49% to ~18% YoY) as large one-off government contracts lapped and commercial slowed with the macro; the next-FY revenue guide implies further deceleration to ~15-17%.

US commercial customer count grew 79% YoY off a small base (80 -> 143), but US commercial REVENUE grew only ~12% YoY in the latest quarter — the new-customer cohort has not yet converted into large revenue.

Government business remains the anchor: trailing-twelve-month government revenue is growing ~20% and defense/intelligence budgets in its home market are rising; the company is embedded in several allied-government programs.

Bear case: stock comp is ~30% of revenue and the share count is up ~35% since listing ~2.5 years ago; separately, ~1,350 invested in ~two dozen small speculative newly-listed companies that promised to buy its software is down ~75% (~1,000 of cumulative losses), the program has been discontinued, and some of that customer cohort's revenue is at risk.

Sell-side consensus is skeptical: at ~8.5x trailing sales with teens growth, most models see the multiple as still above the de-rated peer median and treat the profit print as an expense-management artifact rather than an inflection.
analyst_reports.macro_context: The past year saw the fastest central-bank tightening cycle in decades; unprofitable/high-multiple software de-rated 60-80% from highs; the market currently pays up only for profitable growth.
